lead:
Veteran actor Olu Jacobs died at 84, after years of false reports of his death online, and the Federal Government said his legacy would never fade.

The day in brief: his family confirmed the death of the man they called “The Lion of Lufodo”. The National Assembly sent the Sixth Alteration Bill on state police to the 36 state assemblies and asked for their decisions within 30 days, and the Supreme Court reserved judgment on INEC's appeal to restore voided parts of the Electoral Act 2026. A judge let Atiku Abubakar serve his eligibility suit on President Tinubu through the APC. ASUU began an indefinite strike at Lagos State's three universities, and the outgoing Operation Hadin Kai commander said troops killed more than 1,106 Boko Haram and ISWAP fighters in his 17 months. Tinubu ordered identity number coverage raised to 95 per cent by December, Dangote promised small investors priority in his refinery IPO, and the Kano PDP named Muhammad Sani Abacha its governorship candidate. Nairobi won the right to host the 2029 World Athletics Championships, the first African city to do so.

items.h: Veteran actor Olu Jacobs dies
items.s: Nollywood veteran Olu Jacobs died on Wednesday, 16 September, at the age of 84, his family said; his son Olusoji announced the death of “The Lion of Lufodo”. False reports of his death had circulated online several times in recent years. Culture Minister Hannatu Musawa called his passing a monumental loss to the creative industry and said his legacy would never fade.

items.h: Constitution amendment bill sent to state assemblies
items.s: The National Assembly transmitted the Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, which provides for state police services, to the Houses of Assembly of the 36 states and asked for their resolutions within 30 days. The Clerk acted on the leadership's directive; approval by at least two-thirds of the states is required before the amendment can proceed.

items.h: Supreme Court reserves judgment on Electoral Act appeal
items.s: A seven-member panel of the Supreme Court led by Justice Adamu Jauro reserved judgment on INEC's appeal against the Court of Appeal ruling that voided Sections 77(5), (6) and (7) and 84(2) of the Electoral Act 2026, which deal with party membership registers and the nomination of candidates for 2027.

items.h: Court lets Atiku serve certificate suit on Tinubu through APC
items.s: Justice Inyang Ekwo of the Federal High Court in Abuja granted Atiku Abubakar's ex-parte request to serve court papers on President Tinubu through the APC in the ADC candidate's suit challenging the President's eligibility to contest in 2027, which includes claims over his certificates.

items.h: ASUU begins indefinite strike at three Lagos state universities
items.s: ASUU's joint campus group declared an indefinite strike at Lagos State University, Lagos State University of Education and Lagos State University of Science and Technology after a 14-day ultimatum expired. The union is demanding the implementation of the 2025 agreement with the federal government and action on salaries and retirement benefits.

items.h: Commander says 1,106 terrorists killed in Borno in 17 months
items.s: Major General Abdulsalam Abubakar, outgoing theatre commander of Operation Hadin Kai, said troops killed more than 1,106 Boko Haram and ISWAP fighters during his 17 months in Borno, including over 350 commanders such as Abu Bilal Al-Muniki, and arrested 758 suspected logistics suppliers.

items.h: Tinubu orders 95% NIN coverage by December
items.s: At the 2026 National Identity Day in Abuja, President Tinubu, represented by chief of staff Femi Gbajabiamila, directed NIMC to raise identity number enrolment from about 142 million people to 95 per cent of the population by December 2026, as part of building an integrated digital identity system.

items.h: IGP visits Plateau as three vigilantes are killed
items.s: Inspector-General Olatunji Disu paid a condolence visit to the Plateau government after recent killings and promised stronger police operations and justice for victims. On Tuesday night three vigilantes were killed in NTV community, Barkin Ladi.

items.h: Sanusi says he was wrong to delay telcos' entry into finance
items.s: Former CBN governor and current Emir of Kano, Muhammadu Sanusi II, said at the launch of the 2026 Access to Financial Services survey in Abuja that he was wrong to delay the entry of telecom companies into financial services while at the central bank, a decision he said slowed financial inclusion.

items.h: Dangote promises retail investors priority if IPO is oversubscribed
items.s: Aliko Dangote said retail investors would get priority in allocation if the refinery IPO is oversubscribed, saying the offer was designed to spread ownership of one of Africa's most strategic industrial assets. Banks reported heavy traffic on their subscription channels, and Coronation chairman Aigboje Aig-Imoukhuede called the launch a landmark for African capital markets.

items.h: PDP picks Abacha's son as Kano governorship candidate
items.s: Kano's PDP made Muhammad Sani Abacha, a son of the late military ruler, its governorship flag-bearer after Muhammad Bello Dalha, who had won the ticket, pulled out. The state party chairman, Bello Gambo Bichi, told an enlarged executive meeting on Wednesday that the substitution followed the party's rules.

items.h: Shettima says only six northern governors backed Tinubu in 2023
items.s: Speaking in Ilorin at the turbaning of Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq as Sardauna of Ilorin, Vice President Kashim Shettima said only six of the 19 northern governors backed Tinubu's bid for the APC ticket in 2023, but that the President forgave those who opposed him, and urged Kwara politicians to reconcile.

items.h: Rift between Wike and APC governors deepens
items.s: An APC grassroots group accused FCT Minister Nyesom Wike of trying to divide the party and criticised his remarks about Imo Governor Hope Uzodimma, chairman of the Progressives Governors Forum. Wike's PDP allies said his support is for Tinubu, not the APC, and accused some governors of underperforming, in a rift reflecting deeper battles over influence and succession.

items.h: Adebayo warns petrol could reach N5,000 under a second Tinubu term
items.s: Adewole Adebayo, the SDP's presidential candidate, warned that petrol could rise to as much as N5,000 a litre if President Tinubu wins a second term, blaming the direction of the government's economic policies, in a statement from his campaign.

items.h: APM says regional commission funds could sway votes
items.s: The Allied Peoples Movement said President Tinubu's order to release funds to the regional development commissions could be used to induce voters before 2027. Its spokesman Yusuf Abubakar said the party did not oppose the release but wanted transparency safeguards, measurable deliverables and independent monitoring.

items.h: ADC and APC trade blame over Kaduna attacks
items.s: The ADC said supporters gathered to welcome its Kaduna governorship candidate, Isa Ashiru, back from the lesser Hajj were attacked at a toll gate on Tuesday and some vehicles damaged. The Kaduna APC, through spokesman Sani Dan Azare, condemned attacks on its members and offices and asked the police to investigate.

items.h: Six SDP supporters die in Nasarawa crash
items.s: Six supporters of Mohammed Adamu, the former Inspector-General who is the SDP's governorship candidate in Nasarawa, died in a crash on the Lafia flyover on Monday shortly after leaving the party secretariat on Jos Road for an event in Awe, police said.

items.h: Oba of Benin backs continuity
items.s: Receiving an APC campaign delegation led by director-general Abdulaziz Yari, the Oba of Benin, Ewuare II, urged Nigerians to support continuity in government, saying there is no point in seeking change for its own sake, but added that his remarks should not be read as backing any party.

items.h: 'Arewa for Asiwaju' group to be unveiled
items.s: A coalition of northern leaders, including former governors Ibrahim Shekarau, Ibrahim Geidam and Simon Lalong, prepared to unveil “Arewa for Asiwaju”, a platform to mobilise the North-West, North-East and North-Central for President Tinubu's re-election, led by a 14-member board of trustees.

items.h: APC and ADC field the most National Assembly candidates
items.s: INEC data show the APC fielded the most House of Representatives candidates, 360, followed by the ADC with 346, while the ADC has the most Senate candidates, as parties prepare for the 2027 National Assembly elections.

items.h: Solar mini-grid commissioned at Yakubu Gowon University
items.s: A 3.3-megawatt-peak solar plant with 2MWh of batteries, its own grid link and a training workshop for renewable energy now serves Yakubu Gowon University, the former University of Abuja. The government commissioned it under phase two of the Energizing Education Programme, which covers seven universities and two teaching hospitals.

items.h: Power minister asks EFCC to tackle vandalism and energy theft
items.s: Power Minister Joseph Tegbe asked the EFCC, during a visit to its chairman Ola Olukoyede, to help tackle vandalism and energy theft in the power sector, and complained that some companies with electricity fail to pay their bills, costing the country billions of naira a year.

items.h: Farm produce inflation reaches 21.99%, highest this year
items.s: Farm produce inflation rose to 21.99 per cent year on year in August, its highest level this year, according to NBS data, reversing a slowdown that took it to 13.26 per cent in May before it climbed to 21.70 per cent in June and eased to 19.82 per cent in July.

items.h: Stocks gain N650bn as market value hits N158trn
items.s: The Nigerian Exchange's All-Share Index rose 1,005.27 points, or 0.41 per cent, to 244,304.51 on Tuesday, and market capitalisation gained about N650 billion to close at N158.399 trillion, driven by gains in medium and large companies.

items.h: JAMB moves 2027 UTME first-session arrival to 7.30am
items.s: JAMB moved the arrival time for the first session of the 2027 UTME to 7.30am, citing safety and logistics. Registrar Segun Aina also admitted that the exam has changed little in more than 30 years and may no longer select candidates effectively, as he inaugurated a committee to overhaul it.

items.h: Tinubu makes ending child labour a national priority
items.s: President Tinubu declared ending child labour a national development priority, saying it affects education, poverty reduction, food security and national security, at a national dialogue on the child labour policy in Abuja. SGF George Akume urged governors, employers and communities to act.

items.h: Kano anti-corruption commission chairman resigns
items.s: Saidu Yahaya resigned as chairman of the Kano Public Complaints and Anti-Corruption Commission. Reports said the state government was dissatisfied with his performance, while the Kwankwasiyya movement said he quit because he was prevented from working independently.

items.h: Kano police recover 12 stolen cars and arrest 10
items.s: Kano police arrested 10 suspected members of an interstate car theft ring and recovered 12 stolen vehicles in operations in Kano and neighbouring states by the special intervention squad, Commissioner Ibrahim Adamu Bakori said.

items.h: Seven kidnap victims rescued in Benue
items.s: Operation Whirl Stroke troops, working with police and vigilantes, rescued seven kidnap victims from a hideout around Amla-Icho, Ogobia and Anpekchi in Otukpo and Ohimini, Benue, in an intelligence-led operation on Monday.

items.h: PenCom extends verification deadline to 31 December
items.s: PenCom extended to 31 December 2026 the deadline for the mandatory online verification of federal workers entitled to accrued pension rights, after only 31,099 of about 150,000 eligible employees had enrolled by July. The exercise began in February.

items.h: Airlines blame congestion and weather for delays
items.s: Airlines told an aviation session at the Akwaaba African Travel Market in Lagos that crowded airports, weak facilities and weather account for much of the disruption passengers suffer, and that many of the problems are outside their control. They were reacting to NCAA figures showing six in ten domestic flights left late in August.

items.h: CAC proposes single beneficial ownership database
items.s: CAC Registrar-General Hussaini Ishaq Magaji called for the country's beneficial ownership records to be harmonised in a central database, saying fragmented records across agencies weaken the fight against corruption, money laundering, terrorism financing and abuse of company structures.

items.h: Kwara governor turbanned as Sardauna
items.s: Kwara Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq was turbanned as Sardauna of Ilorin on Wednesday, a title first made famous by Sir Ahmadu Bello, the Premier of Northern Nigeria, in a ceremony at the palace of the Emir of Ilorin attended by Vice President Shettima.

items.h: Zamfara governor to attend UN General Assembly
items.s: Zamfara Governor Dauda Lawal will attend the 81st UN General Assembly in New York to meet partners and seek investment for the state, starting with a high-level roundtable and the SDG Moment on 18 September.

items.h: Nairobi beats London, Munich and Rome to 2029 World Athletics hosting
items.s: World Athletics chose Nairobi to host the 2029 World Championships over London, Munich and Rome, making it the first African city to stage the event. Munich got 2031. President Sebastian Coe said Nairobi presented “a compelling and emotional bid”.

items.h: World Bank names Michael Kremer chief economist
items.s: World Bank President Ajay Banga appointed Nobel laureate Michael Kremer as chief economist and senior vice president for development economics, to lead the bank's research, data and analysis.
